title: Empty Islands
scope: Public SuperCC comparison with the existing Tile World MS reference; no claim about CHIP.EXE authority.

probes.name: exact-tws-import
probes.input: Unmodified 147-byte replay through public TWSReader and Solution.load

probes.name: absolute-target-control
probes.input: Same replay; observation subclass supplies absolute target (0,10) at half tick371, bypassing relative target conversion for that click. Engine source unchanged.

divergences.name: relative mouse target is anchored at a different point in the tick
divergences.observedEffect: SuCC resolves relative177=(0,-1) from pre-forced-movement position (0,12), targeting (0,11). Tile World reconstructs it after its forced movement to (0,11), targeting (0,10).
divergences.sourceExplanation: TWSReader correctly decodes the relative pair; Solution.tickBasicMoves turns it into an absolute click before calling the engine. Tile World floormovements precedes choosemove and relative mouse expansion.

divergences.name: same-direction voluntary mouse movement on a force floor is suppressed
divergences.observedEffect: Even when the probe supplies intended absolute goal (0,10), SuCC advances only to (0,11); the goal remains (0,10).
divergences.sourceExplanation: MSLevel rejects CLICK_EARLY when the sought direction equals the sliding direction; moveChip repeats that suppression. Tile World tests the raw command against the slide direction before converting a mouse command into a cardinal direction, so the mouse command bypasses that comparison.

reproduction.validation: Script rerun successfully; both expected failures reproduced, exact DAT/replay hashes and replay byte size checked, tracked SuperCC source clean before and after.

limitations: This establishes observable differences between the pinned public SuperCC source and the project's Tile World MS reference. It does not establish which matches the original Microsoft executable.
SuperCC uses half ticks; the observed transition from half371 to half372 corresponds to Tile World processing native tick742.
The absolute-target control deliberately changes one supplied input; it is a control experiment, not the unchanged TWS result.
The probe is a subclass with logging and read-only reflection; SuperCC engine source is not patched.
